author: Robert Carr
description: Skillet-seared all-beef hot dogs with sharp cheddar, golden Worcestershire onions, jalapeno-pickle relish, and chipotle-lime mayo on butter-toasted potato buns.
equipment: 12-inch stainless steel or cast-iron skillet with a lid

groceryIngredients.note: Fully cooked, bun-length franks, about 3 oz each; natural casing or skinless.
Or regular soft hot dog buns.
Four thin slices, about 1/2 oz each.
Or another neutral high-heat cooking oil.
One medium onion, about 6 to 8 oz.
Use 1 small pepper, about 2 tsp minced, plus 1 tsp adobo sauce from the same can.

ingredients: 4 fully cooked, bun-length all-beef hot dogs, about 3 oz each; natural casing preferred, or skinless
2 oz sharp cheddar, cut into 4 thin slices
2 tablespoons unsalted butter, divided; soften 1 tablespoon for the buns
2 teaspoons avocado oil or another neutral high-heat oil, divided
1 medium yellow onion, about 6 to 8 oz, halved and thinly sliced crosswise
1/8 teaspoon kosher salt, for the onions
1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, for the onions
3 tablespoons drained pickled jalapenos, chopped into small pieces
3 tablespoons drained dill pickles, chopped into small pieces
1 small chipotle pepper in adobo, finely minced (about 2 teaspoons), plus 1 teaspoon adobo sauce from the same can
Water, as needed for reheating the franks and loosening the onions
instructions: Stir together 3 tablespoons mayonnaise, 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard, 1 minced chipotle pepper, 1 teaspoon adobo sauce, 1 teaspoon lime juice, and 1/8 teaspoon garlic powder in a small bowl. In a second bowl, combine 3 tablespoons chopped pickled jalapenos and 3 tablespoons chopped dill pickles, blotting away excess brine. Refrigerate both while you cook.

Heat 1 tablespoon butter and 1 teaspoon oil in the skillet over medium heat. Add the sliced onion, 1/8 teaspoon kosher salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Cook for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and golden brown. Lower the heat if the edges darken too quickly, and add a splash of water to loosen browned bits as needed. Stir in 1 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce and cook for 30 to 60 seconds, until no liquid remains. Transfer the onions to a plate and keep warm.

While the onions cook, heat the 4 hot dogs in enough barely simmering water to cover them, about 8 to 12 minutes, until steaming hot throughout and the centers reach 165 degrees F. Follow any higher temperature listed on the package. Keep the water below a rolling boil and leave the casings intact.

Wipe any scorched onion residue from the skillet and return it to medium heat. Spread the remaining 1 tablespoon softened butter over the cut sides of the 4 buns. Toast cut-side down for 1 to 2 minutes, working in batches as needed, until golden. Set the buns cut-side up, uncovered, so the toasted surfaces stay crisp.

Remove the hot dogs from the water and pat them thoroughly dry. Heat the remaining 1 teaspoon oil in the skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Sear the hot dogs for 2 to 3 minutes total, turning with tongs, until browned in several places. Lower the heat if the casings start to swell, and stop before they split.
Reduce the heat to low and lay 1 thin slice of cheddar lengthwise over each hot dog. Cover for 30 to 60 seconds, just until the cheese softens and melts, then remove the hot dogs from the skillet.

Spread about 1 tablespoon chipotle mayo inside each toasted bun. Add a cheese-topped hot dog, about 2 tablespoons onions, and 1 to 1 1/2 tablespoons drained jalapeno-pickle relish. Serve immediately, with extra toppings on the side.
notes: Natural-casing all-beef hot dogs give a firmer snap; skinless franks also work. Do not slash or spiral-cut them before cooking.
For milder heat, use half the chipotle and replace half the pickled jalapenos with dill pickle. For more heat, add another chipotle and replace some of the dill pickle with hot pickled jalapenos.
Use soft buns that fit the hot dogs and thin slices of sharp cheddar that melt quickly. Keep the toppings light enough that the beef still comes through.
For a grill finish, warm and dry the hot dogs as directed, then brown briefly over medium-high heat, turning often. Move to indirect heat to melt the cheese and toast the buns separately.

The mayo, relish, and onions can be made a day ahead and refrigerated separately at 40 degrees F or colder. Reheat the onions until steaming hot and cook off excess moisture. Toast the buns and finish the hot dogs just before serving. Refrigerate perishable leftovers within 2 hours, or within 1 hour above 90 degrees F.
title: Spicy Beef Hot Dogs
